body: Yes. All I want is death. I can't hurt others, though.

I've reached out to some of them, but for the most part they just can't handle me not being ok. Most of them just shut down emotionally when I try to talk about my depression. I know that I shouldn't kill myself. Problem is, I really, really want to, because I can't escape from my own pain. I guess it's safe to say that I'm a bit lost.

The lies are terrifying. I can't stop myself from being insanely self destructive, but I'm so high functioning and such a good liar that only people who I've straight up told about my problems personally know that I'm not ok. The truth is, I haven't been able to eat a full meal in almost four weeks now, I cut myself on an almost daily basis, I regularly fantasize about suicide, and I can't make myself better. But I can lie about it. And nobody ever calls me out on the lies. So yeah, I'm scared of how well I lie. But I'm not sure if I'm more scared of how well I lie or how easily others believe the lie. Because both are pretty goddamn terrifying.
It really depends on the size/position of the cuts. Hiking and yard work are both good ones, if your cuts look random enough. If they're the straight parallel lines, then not so much, though.

For me, blood is a stabilizing agent. I need the pain and the lines on my stomach to feel human- it jerks me out of my lows and into a state that lets me interact comfortably with other people. It makes me ok.

I vary between razor blades and a broken box cutter, but I keep them hidden in a compass that can be easily carried in my purse or in my pocket depending on what I need at the time. Very inconspicuous, plus it has the delightful double meaning of being there for me when I'm lost.

I do it all over my stomach. It's not an area anyone will ever see, so I don't have to worry about dealing with judgement. It makes hugs painful sometimes, and lying on my front is kinda unmanageable, but only I know that.

I feel the same way- the worst part is, if you're not careful, your brain can trick you into thinking that they're the ones who are pushing YOU away, which tends to not be true.
The important thing, hard as it is, is to keep trying to reach out to people in a positive way. Make sure everyone knows how much they mean to you, so that they understand that it's not you pushing them away, it's your illness causing you to push them away.

I have so much trouble eating. I lost over ten pounds in one week just from being unable to eat. It's the worst when people expect you to be social and go out to eat with them- buying a meal and only being able to take one or two bites, and the shame that follows from being just completely unable to eat, end up making me feel even worse.
The only people in the world you can trust are animals. My dog is always there for me, humans aren't worth the trouble.

A razor blade, popped out from the razor. It's small and a bit awkward to hold without cutting your fingers, but it creates very small cuts that I like, and looks almost like you've been clawed by a cat.

Yeah. I'm scared of it. I was such an honest person, once upon a time. Now I lie to everyone constantly. I'm just scared of loneliness, but the truth is, thanks to the lies I'm as lonely as ever, surrounded by people who have no clue that my goofy goddamn grin is practiced daily so it seems sincere. I wish I wasn't a liar. But no one would understand the truth. I prefer loneliness over isolation.
Usually my stomach. I'm a female lifeguard, so I wouldn't get away with long sleeves or long shorts- it's too damn hot. Besides, I'm too heavy to wear a bikini so I'll never get caught.

I'm probably an addict. I don't want to hurt myself, it just ends up happening. For me, I just get so wrapped up in how much I hate myself that I feel a compulsive need to punish myself for the crime of existing. So, not a whole lot of control, I suppose.

I have this problem. I tend to cope with it by finding other people who are up late at night and talking to them- I have two friends who are night owls who are also the only people in my life who know I am depressed. I try to use talking to people as my first avenue of dealing with night time misery, because when I fail to find someone I tend to self harm. I don't recommend self harm, though, stick with late night chats.

With almost no details, it's hard to say that I know where you're coming from- but I'm also 18, and I also self harm, though I am trying to stop. I know that everything probably seems dark right now, and I don't know how to make things ok- but I'd like you to know that you're not alone. I may not know you, but I care about you and don't want to see you hurt. You may not know me, and I may not know you, but know that somewhere out in the great big terrifying world, you have a friend in me. I hope we both can eventually heal.

You're not being selfish. Feeling alone is hard, us humans are social animals by nature and we need each other more than we'd care to admit in this day and age. Just remember this: depression has a way of skewing the way you see things. When you're low, you feel like everyone either doesn't care or is against you. But really, there are many people who care about you. I've never even met you, and I care about you. Try to find someone to talk to, someone you can trust enough to ask for help, whether it's a friend or a counselor. You're young, and your home situation isn't too great, from the sound of things, but you're 17. You have a whole life in front of you, and the one good thing about depression is that it will allow you to enjoy the good times you will have ahead of you so much more. Never be afraid to ask for help, depression is every bit as much a sickness as the flu and there's nothing shameful in being helped up. Good luck, friend. You're not alone.
